Adjust the angle of the stitch with the flipped Cultural Ruler.

chunks.title: [CLO Official Tutorial Video - Basic Series p04 4. Making Pants]
chunks.content: # CLO Official Tutorial: Making Women's Pants (Basic Series p04) This document details the step-by-step process of creating women's pants in CLO software, covering model setup, panel arrangement, sewing techniques, stitching, simulation, and fabric application. It includes instructions on using CLO’s 2D and 3D windows, adjustment tools, sewing tools, and simulation features to design and simulate pants accurately. --- ## 1. Setting Up the Female Model and Workspace This section explains how to import a female avatar and prepare the workspace for pants creation, focusing on model selection, panel framing, and arrangement visualization. - Open CLO and double-click in the screen window. - Navigate to **FemaleVR** and double-click to load the female avatar. - Drag the model into the 3D window. - Open the folder path: **B > BASIC > D > PANTS > FEMALES**. - Drag the camera into the 3D window, confirm the dialog box by clicking OK. - In the 2D window, use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** to frame all pants panels, focusing on placing the panel and model shadow properly (only half of the panel visible initially). - Frame the back panel using the same adjustment tool. - Right-click on the panel, select **Column Link Panel**, align panels with frame lines, hold Shift, and set the mirrored panel on the opposite side. - In the 3D toolbar, select all positions to frame the 2D arrangement and transfer this arrangement to the 3D window. - In the 3D vertical bar, enable **Display Arrangement Point** to visualize arrangement points; note any blocked arrangements. - In the 2D window, select all panels and move them up or down to identify blocked arrangement points in the 3D window. --- ## 2. Panel Positioning and Symmetry This section covers positioning separate panels such as pockets and front panels, and creating symmetrical duplicates of pants panels. - The pocket and front panel are separate pieces. - In the 3D window, select the pocket panel and use the **Position Tool** to move it behind the front panel. - Select the left front panel and move it on top of the right front panel using the Position Tool. - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** in the 2D window to move and align the left front panel precisely. - Hold Shift and select the front pocket and pocket panels. - Use the **Carolina panel** option in the menu to create symmetrical panels, copying the other half of the pants and pockets. - Hold Shift to place the duplicated panels horizontally on the opposite side. - Use the **Edit Panel Tool** while holding Shift to select front pocket and pocket panels for adjustment. - In the 3D window, place panels at arrangement points by clicking the left mouse button on the model’s arrangement points. - Adjust panel positions using the purple column arranged by mouse control. - Hold Shift and select left and right waist panels simultaneously; place them at the forefoot arrangement point in the 3D window.

Sewing Panels and Creating Seams This section details the use of sewing tools to join panels, change seam types, and simulate realistic pockets and pants structures. - Use the **Free-Default Tool** to combine the pocket and jade panels with the pants panel. - At the junction where pocket and pants panels meet, create a sewing line. - Change the sewing line type to **Turned** in the application editor to achieve a flatter pocket appearance during simulation. - Use the **Sewing Tool** to stitch the front and side parts of the pants. - Activate the **MBM Free Sewing** option by long-pressing the Free-Default Tool. - Combine side parts as needed and press Return to complete sewing. - Use the Sewing Tool to sew the back waist and back waist panel. - Sew the waist panel to both the pocket and pants panels. - In the 3D window, select the stitch tool. - On the 2D panel, click the stitch button on the left to add stitches; the stitch line appears on the 2D pattern and the corresponding stitched area appears on the 3D model. - Use the **Move Tool** to select and adjust stitch angles using the **Flipped Cultural Ruler**. --- ## 4. Adding Buttons and Belt Panels This section explains how to add buttons and adjust belt panels with natural hanging behavior. - In the 3D toolbar, select the **Button Tool**. - In the 2D window, click the button icon, then click the button to toggle visibility (close the eye icon) twice to finalize. - Select the belt panel using the Adjustment Panel Tool. - In the View menu, find **Sticky Stick** option; click the arrow next to it, select the sticky box, and click the fire icon to make the panel hang naturally on the virtual model. --- ## 5.

Simulation and Fabric Application This section covers running physical simulations, improving garment quality, and applying fabric textures to the pants. - After completing sewing and panel arrangement, activate the simulation. - Once simulation is applied and complete, turn off the simulation. - Enter the **Canvas Window**, double-click the **AVAILABLE** file, then open the **FemaleValue** file. - Double-click to open the **POS** file and confirm by clicking the AVAILABLE button. - Within the POS file, select **FV203** or drag it into the 3D window. - Confirm via the menu and change the model’s posture to vertical. - Enter the drawing window and double-click the **Fabric** file. - Double-click on the **Carton Coupling** fabric file and drag it into the Fabric window. - This applies a 7-way simulation to the 3D clothing, improving fabric drape and realism. - In the 3D window, select the tool to improve clothing quality and confirm the dialog box. - The improved simulation will be applied to the 3D clothing, enhancing appearance and fit. --- # Summary This tutorial guides through setting up a female model in CLO, manipulating 2D and 3D pants panels, achieving symmetrical panel placement, sewing with appropriate seam types, adding buttons and belts with natural physics, and applying fabric simulations. The process integrates CLO’s powerful adjustment, sewing, and simulation tools to create realistic and accurately fitted pants for virtual clothing design.
